tasks.title: PTC interrupt rating: F1/F3/F4 100 A PTC + series resistor, then the F2 swap
tasks.brief: Owner ruling Q-0047 (verbatim): "(a) - 1812 60 V PTC with Imax 100 A (TECHFUSE mSMD050-60V C70113 or JDT ASMD1812-050-60V C427396, same footprint) after a datasheet check, plus a series resistor of about 0.15-0.22 ohm per PTC so that 30 V / R_total <= Imax; check the resistor's pulse energy against the PTC trip time, and if no basic/cheap part passes, return to the owner; then do the dependent F2 swap (T-0026); F4 is safety-relevant, so a competent person reviews it before installation". Background: docs/reviews/2026-11-02-fix-shared-T-0065.md (1812L050/60GR I_max 40 A, R_min 0.150 ohm, prospective short 30 V / 0.16 ohm = 188 A). Shared change, identical on both boards: F1 (power-usb, VS feed to the buck), F3 (can, NET-S feed), F4 (analog_sw, VS -> F4 -> D55 -> SW_SUPPLY/J5.5), F2 (power-usb, USB VBUS J3 -> F2 -> FB1/C4). Steps in order: 1) part_facts.py C70113 and C427396: I_max at V_max (must be >= 100 A at >= 30 V, V_max 60 V), I_hold/I_trip at 25 and 60 C (I_hold 0.5 A class as now; F1 carries the buck input current, F4 about 50-55 mA), R_min/R1max, time-to-trip curve, package 1812 matching the present 1812 footprint, JLCPCB class/price/stock. Pick the one that passes and is cheaper (basic/preferred first). 2) Series resistor per PTC on F1, F3, F4: R_series >= 30 V / I_max - R_min(PTC) (do not count cable or terminals), E24 value in the 0.15-0.22 ohm range of the ruling. Pulse energy check: from the PTC time-to-trip at the prospective current (30 V / (R_min + R_series)) take I^2*t, then E = I^2*t*R_series; compare it with the resistor's short-time overload / single-pulse rating from its datasheet (part_facts.py). Also check the continuous dissipation and drop at I_hold, and that the extra drop in the F4 path (about 10 mV at 55 mA) does not change the SWIN margin in design-notes section 3. Prefer a basic 1206 or 2512 thick-film or a current-sense chip resistor; one part type for all three positions. 3) Edit with tools/ksch.py: F1/F3/F4 value, LCSC and footprint (if the 1812 footprint differs, verify it against the package drawing); add one series resistor next to each of F1, F3, F4 on the supply side, so that the TVS stays at the connector side. 4) Dependent F2 swap (T-0026, decision 32): F2 SMD0805B050TF C269104 -> the same PTC part as F1/F3/F4, footprint 0805 -> 1812 (Fuse_1812). F2 is on 5 V USB VBUS (host-limited), so the ruling's series resistor is not needed there. Check I_hold against the USB current. 5) ERC and netlist on both boards before/after: only F1-F4 and the three new resistors (with their new nets) may differ. Run tools/fix_check.py --scope shared. 6) Documents: design-notes section 8.3 (calculation, part facts, failure mode: a hard short at J5.5 or on NET-S now limited to <= I_max, F4 trips and disables the panel switches while bus control keeps working), ARCHITECTURE power-usb/analog_sw rows if they name the PTC (not the invariants), both STATUS files (drop the 'Blocked: PTC' paragraph and the pre-order item 'Resolve the F1/F3/F4 PTC I_max question'; note that F2 is now swapped). Safety note in the report and STATUS: F4 feeds the panel switches (bilge forced run, navigation lights); a competent person reviews F1/F3/F4 before installation. Stop and ask (one-way): if neither C70113 nor C427396 shows I_max >= 100 A at >= 30 V in its datasheet, or neither fits the 1812 footprint; if no basic/cheap resistor passes the pulse-energy check (the ruling says return to the owner); if the series resistor would cut the SWIN margin in design-notes section 3 below 2.0 V.

tasks.title: Short EMC gate slew, maximum load capacitance, HC2 load guidance
tasks.brief: Owner rulings (verbatim). Q-0049 (T-0054): "(1) maximum load capacitance: rate HC2 for about 50-100 uF load input capacitance, confirmed by the prototype measurement (Q-0045); fit only a short gate slew for EMC (within the MOSFET SOA at that capacitance); README: HC2 is for motor loads (bilge pumps, wipers) and grouped LED work lights, while DC-DC converters (e.g. 24->12 V for a car radio), radios and other electronics go on the 4-channel board; split grouped LED lights if the prototype shows short-circuit trips". Q-0050 (T-0006): "covered by Q-0049: short EMC-only gate slew within the MOSFET SOA". Q-0051 (T-0061): "typical HC2 loads are bilge pumps and wipers (not capacitive) and possibly grouped 100 W LED work lights (a few hundred uF in total); DC-DC converters for 12 V car radios, radios and other electronics go on the 4-channel board; see Q-0049". Q-0053 (T-0053): "no - drop the 21 A option; decision 19 is withdrawn by the owner (2026-11-03); the breaker stays as in decision 39". These amend the 1000 uF / 20 A sizing of decision 25; its topology stays (TPS4811-Q1 section 8.3.2.1 / Fig. 8-6: R1 in the PU path = R104/R204, C1 + about 10 ohm at the gate, PD direct, RGATE_PD as a 0 ohm footprint). Inputs: docs/part-facts/C17556513.md (Eq. 3 I_inrush = 0.63 x V(BST-SRC) x C_LOAD / (R1 x C1), Eq. 4 CBST > Qg + 10 x C1, tSC 4/5 us), docs/part-facts/C501507.md (BSC030N08NS5 SOA Diagram 3 at 30 V: 10 us ~185 A, 100 us ~15 A; Zth Diagram 4), and the method and script of docs/reviews/2026-11-02-fix-pdm-hc2-T-0070.md. Steps: 1) Size R1/C1 so that ALL of these hold at 30 V: (a) with C_LOAD = 100 uF (aim) plus a 15 A resistive load, inrush + load stays below the minimum ISCP threshold (about 71 A with RISCP 4.7 k) with margin, so the fast trip does not fire at turn-on; (b) the input-side MOSFET Q11/Q21 stays inside SOA Diagram 3 and Tj < 150 C from Zth for that ramp, starting from the hot case and from a retry after running at 15 A (heat budget); (c) turn-on into a hard short (slow gate rise, 30 V across Q11 until ISCP trips plus tSC) stays inside SOA - T-0070 showed 100 k / 3.9 nF fails this; (d) the output dV/dt is far below today's 400-800 V/us (EMC report 2026-10-30, E2; PROFET reference 0.8 V/us), ramp in the tens of microseconds; (e) Eq. 4 with the existing CBST; (f) turn-off unchanged (PD direct). If 100 uF cannot meet (a)-(c), take the largest C_LOAD between 50 and 100 uF that does, and state it as the rating. Prefer R/C values and parts already on the BOM (e.g. C1523 1 nF, C25744 10 k, C25076 100 ohm). 2) tools/ksch.py on hc_channel (both channels): R104/R204 value = R1, add C1 + 10 ohm at the gate and the 0 ohm RGATE_PD footprint per decision 25. ERC and netlist before/after; only these refs may change. fix_check.py --scope pdm-hc2. 3) Rerun tools/heat_budget.py --channels 2 --part HC-2xBSC030 at 40 C (rating stays about 15 A; no PWM). 4) README: in the boards/limitations text, HC2 is for motor loads (bilge pumps, wipers) and grouped LED work lights; DC-DC converters (e.g. 24->12 V for a car radio), radios and other electronics go on pdm-4ch; give the maximum load input capacitance; split grouped LED work lights if they trip. Keep the existing no-PWM and timing bullets. 5) design-notes section 4a: sizing, SOA/Zth calculation, the rating, and a failure-mode note for bilge forced-run outputs (slew does not delay the fast trip; a large capacitive load trips and waits 3.8 min; a competent person reviews the bilge outputs before installation). 6) hardware/pdm-hc2/STATUS.md: replace the T-0070 'blocked' paragraph and Next item 0 with the result. Prototype test list: measure the real load capacitance and inrush of each intended HC2 load, including grouped LED work lights (Q-0045), confirm the 50-100 uF rating, and split LED groups that trip. T-0053: R113/R213 stay 68 k C36871 (decision 39, T-0072), no change; note that decision 19 and the 21 A option are withdrawn. Stop and ask (one-way): if no R1/C1 meets (a)-(c) even at 50 uF; if meeting them would need a change to RISCP/the fast-trip level, the breaker (decision 39), CBST or the MOSFET (decision 19 is withdrawn); if the heat budget moves the 15 A rating.

tasks.title: pdm-4ch reverse-battery blocking on VS in front of the bulk capacitor
tasks.brief: Owner ruling Q-0054 (verbatim): "Add reverse blocking now, this revision: a reverse-blocking element (P-FET or ideal-diode controller) on VS in front of the bulk capacitors on pdm-4ch, sized for the 40-50 A path and checked with the heat budget at 40 C. Until it is in, limit the README/design-notes claim to the BTT6050 and warn that C31 is not reverse-rated. Still key J10 (decision 34)." Finding: EMC E16 in docs/reviews/2026-11-03-emc-system.md. pdm-4ch only: HC2 keeps decision 40, and C106/C206 are not in scope. Steps in order. (1) Interim text first, so it stands even if a later step stops: README line 47 and design-notes section 8 (T-0050 paragraph). The reversal survival applies to the BTT6050 switches only; C31 (C487384, polarised electrolytic) is not reverse-rated and can overheat and vent. (2) Topology. Put the element between the VBAT_IN/JP30-FL30 side and VS, as a new intermediate net. D30 and C30 stay on VBAT_IN at J10. Everything on VS (C31, C104-C404, U11-U14, F1, F4, R60) sits behind it. Requirements: (a) It works without the ESP32 and without 3.3 V (invariant 1; the panel switch supply F4 hangs on VS). (b) Invariant 3: Vds >= 60 V for the 48.4 V D30 clamp, and Vgs protected (zener) where the gate sees the battery. (c) Invariant 4: positive PROFET output surges must still reach D30 (OUT -> body diode -> VS -> D30). A P-FET fully on with its gate to GND conducts both ways and keeps this path. An ideal-diode controller that blocks VS -> VBAT_IN breaks it. (d) Keep the turn-on into C31 + C104-C404 inside the FET's SOA. (3) Part. Prefer JLCPCB basic/preferred, then a part already on a BOM, else one extended part; the ruling requires the function. Check every limit with tools/part_facts.py: Vds, Vgs max, Rds(on) at the hot Tj, Id, SOA, RthJA/case and the package drawing for the footprint. Check stock. (4) Heat at 40 C. tools/heat_budget.py with the blocker's hot Rds(on) added to --r-path (or its I^2R loss added to --p-other). Cases: the standard 4 x BTT6050 at 4 A, the --mix BTT6010 case, and the blocker's own Tj at the 40 A input-terminal current. The 4 A (BTT6050) and about 8 A (BTT6010) channel ratings must stand. (5) ERC and netlist. tools/fix_check.py --scope pdm-4ch --refs with every new or changed ref (the parts on the old VS-JP30 node move to the new net). (6) Documents. README and design-notes section 8: the new reverse-battery behaviour (up to the voltage the part allows), and still check the polarity. Failure-mode note: a short-failed blocker means no reverse protection, as today; an open-failed blocker means a dead board, panel switches included (nav lights, bilge forced run; the float circuit stays independent, invariant 8). Remind the owner that a competent person reviews it before installation. pdm-4ch STATUS 'For /system': the ARCHITECTURE root row must mention the pdm-4ch blocker (sync sweep); J10 keyed/polarised on pdm-4ch too (decision 34, /system mechanical); the supply-path budget figure if it changes. PCB rules: copper width for 40 A and heat sinking. STOP and ask (one-way) if: (i) no available part meets 40 A at 40 C inside the heat budget, or the BTT6050 4 A / BTT6010 about 8 A rating would fall; (ii) the chosen topology needs a TVS on VS or other new wording of invariant 4 (no invariant edits); (iii) the path breaks the ARCHITECTURE budget 'shared supply path <= 2 mOhm' and the heat budget does not show that it is harmless; (iv) a part's facts cannot be verified. In each stop case keep step (1) and report the candidate parts.

tasks.title: TVS across Q30 for negative transients with VS charged
tasks.brief:
Owner's ruling Q-0066, verbatim: "Fit a TVS across Q30 (drain VS to source VBAT_FL) on the first order. Choose it so that Q30 VDS stays below 60 V at the pulse current while the TVS takes the energy of a negative transient with VS charged (80-115 mJ, check at the real maximum input of 32 A = 4 x BTT6010 at 8 A); it must not conduct for a steady reversed battery (<= 28 V) or in normal operation. Basic/preferred part if one fits. Correct design-notes 8.6 (b) and adjust the 8.6 (c) wording (the TVS is across Q30, not from VS to GND; the OUT->VS->Q30->D30 surge path stays). Back to the owner if no part keeps VDS below 60 V."

Background: docs/reviews/2026-11-03-emc-system-2.md E18, docs/reviews/2026-11-03-fix-pdm-4ch-T-0132.md, design-notes 8.6, docs/part-facts/C122552.md. The plan report docs/reviews/2026-11-04-plan-system-T-0136.md explains points 1-3 below with tables; its TVS figures are family values from memory, not checked, so verify them.

In order:

1. Part facts first, with tools/part_facts.py. Read SMCJ30CA C19077607 (already on the BOM as D30, no new unique part; the first candidate): VRWM, VBR min/max, VC at Ipp, IR at 28 V, peak pulse power against pulse duration, JLCPCB basic/preferred status. If point 2 or 3 needs a higher clamp, look up the same-family SMCJ36CA, SMCJ40CA and SMCJ43CA with the pcbparts tools or part_facts.py and read their facts. Prefer a basic/preferred part if one fits, as the ruling says. Use a bidirectional CA part: a unidirectional TVS would conduct forward next to Q30's body diode at power-up, and the ruling says no conduction in normal operation. Do not add a second TVS, a series element, or any other extra part or footprint.

2. Pulse current basis. It is not the 32 A load. The TVS current ends in VBAT_IN, so it cannot exceed what the transient source pulls from that node; if it tried to, VBAT_IN would rise and D30 would stop conducting. D30 only holds -48.4 V up to its Ipp, so that model implies a source of at most about 31 A (verify in the D30 facts). Check this reasoning, and if you accept it, use D30's Ipp as the bounding current and state it as an assumption in the design notes. Also give VDS at the textbook ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 source current if you can source that figure, marked as such, and give the T-0132 stiff-clamp figure (VBAT_IN fixed at -48.4 V, current limited only by C31 ESR, 30-300 mOhm) next to it for comparison. C31's ESR has no lower limit in its facts file.

3. Checks for each candidate: (a) VDS below 60 V at the bounding current, using VBR max plus the slope from VC at Ipp, with a margin stated. (b) VRWM at least 28 V, with IR at 28 V: confirm the leakage into VS during a steady reversed battery is harmless (R60 divider about 242 k), and keep the claim of no time limit in 8.6 'Reverse battery now' only if that holds; also update that paragraph for what happens above D30 VBR and with VS charged at the moment of reversal, where the TVS conducts once. (c) Normal operation: no conduction with Q30 on (VDS near 0) or at power-up. (d) Energy: recompute, because the 80-115 mJ was for Q30 avalanching at 60-66 V; a lower clamp takes more from the capacitors, E = C x (VS + 48.4 - Vc) x Vc with C = 109.2 uF and VS = 29 V gives about 150-164 mJ for Vc 39-50 V. Add the energy fed to the loads for the rest of the pulse at the 32 A case (load about 0.75 ohm in total, current falling with VS, bounded by source current x Vc x pulse length) and compare with the part's pulse rating at that duration. (e) VS at the end of the pulse = V(TVS) - V(D30), worst tolerances, at the bounding current and at lower currents. Choose the part that meets (a)-(d) with VS least negative, preferring the part already on the BOM when it also meets (e).

4. Schematic: add one TVS with tools/ksch.py on the pdm-4ch root sheet, next free ref (D31 is free; D30 is the highest D3x), between Q30 drain net VS and source net VBAT_FL, with an LCSC code. No net changes other than the new part's connections. Run ERC and compare the netlist before and after; declare refs: only the new TVS. Change no shared sheet, because this part of the root sheet exists only on pdm-4ch and the controller part stays identical.

5. Heat: the TVS dissipates nothing in steady state, so the heat budget is unchanged. Run tools/heat_budget.py at 40 C with the existing --r-path 0.00505 and --mix case to confirm, as CLAUDE.md requires. Do not change its inputs.

6. Docs, within the package's scope: design-notes 8.6 (b): replace 'VDS <= 48.4 V' with the true statement (steady reversal with VS discharged against a negative transient with VS charged, which the TVS now clamps), with the pulse-current assumption and the T-0130 note that such transients on a real bus are unverified. 8.6 (c): the TVS is across Q30, not from VS to GND; the OUT->VS->Q30->D30 surge path stays; invariant 4 wording unchanged. Add the part to the 8.6 parts table and Cost. Failure modes: TVS short (bypasses Q30: no reverse protection, not visible in use, same as 'Q30 fails short'); TVS open (back to Q30 avalanche, the T-0132 hot-start margin). tasks.brief:
Fourth attempt at T-0218. The board on main is the T-0236 build 2: 74 unconnected, 0 DRC errors, parity 0, VS-In2 1 island, 1185.4 of 1190.7 mm2. Start from main, and first confirm that state with kpcb drc.

Owner's ruling (Q-0071, new decision row amending 172), verbatim: "In2 corridor. Allow signal tracks through the VS copper on In2.Cu only; F.Cu/B.Cu VS, the 16 A paths and the surge path stay unchanged. VS-In2 stays one piece and keeps every PROFET's thermal vias inside it, loses at most 15 % of its baseline area, and the heat budget at 40 °C must pass (tools/heat_budget.py). First fix the router export so the DSN has no built-in violations (T-0236 reports 722), and run several Freerouting runs per build so the run-to-run spread does not hide gains. Route mostly by script: the four output channels are identical, so design one channel's signal bus (sense, input, LED lines) through the In2 corridor once and generate the other three as the same pattern in scripts/fixed_routes.py; the J6 bundle, CAN, USB and the U1 fan-out stay fixed routes too. Freerouting only fills the remaining short links; if it still cannot close them after the export fix, drop it and script those links as well."

Sources:
- docs/reviews/2026-11-12-fix-pdm-4ch-T-0236.md: open items by group, the builds table, the next steps;
- design-notes 8.16 (build method; the 500-700 'unfixable' violations), 8.17 and 8.18 (the west pocket geometry, J6 bundle v2 and the J3 VBUS route, both pre-checked at 0 DRC errors on fixed copper);
- hardware/pdm-4ch/STATUS.md;
- decisions 163-175.

Method (decision 163): fixes go into hardware/pdm-4ch/scripts/ (routing_build.py, fixed_routes.py, build_routing.sh), and the board is the build output. Placement moves, if any, use tools/kpcb.py.

REPORT DISCIPLINE:
- Write the report within the first 10 minutes. Its fix block lists T-0218 under 'blocked' (door two-way, reason 'in progress: <stage>').
- Update the report after each stage.
- Move T-0218 to 'done' only at 0 unconnected.
- Never leave done and blocked both empty.
- Do not commit; the orchestrator does. Leave the best clean state in the worktree, with the scripts reproducing that board. Use LAND_BEST=1 once after fixed_routes.py changes, if needed.

TIME BOX:
- Start each build in the background with a 25-min limit.
- At most 5 builds.
- Stop work at about 75 minutes, keep the best clean state, and finish the report.

STAGE 1 - clean router export (no board change):
1. In routing_build.py prep, find what makes the 722 DSN violations. Suspects from 8.16: power copper inside its own pour keep-out, and pads near the 0.35 mm edge strip.
2. Change the export so the DSN has 0 built-in violations (Freerouting log). Do not loosen any KiCad DRC rule or keep-out to get there.
3. From then on, build with 3 runs (build_routing.sh 3 25). The script already gives each run its own strategy (FR_STRATS).
4. Record the violations before and after, and the 3-run spread.

STAGE 2 - corridor rule (scripts only):
1. Let signal tracks on In2.Cu pass inside the VS-In2 outline: VS-In2 is no longer a track keep-out for foreign nets on In2.
2. Change nothing on F.Cu/B.Cu VS, the VBAT/OUT pours, the 16 A paths or the surge path. Their keep-outs stay exactly as they are.
3. Make the pour check per pour: VS-In2 may lose up to 15 % of its 1190.7 mm2 baseline (so >= 1012 mm2) and must stay 1 island. Every other pour keeps its island count and >= 95 % of its area (decision 172).
4. Add a check that every PROFET thermal via (U11-U14 exposed pad vias, VS) lies inside the filled VS-In2 and is connected to it.
5. Leave the VS-In2 outline unchanged; the fill clears around the tracks.
6. Run one 3-run build and keep it if it is better.

STAGE 3 - scripted channel bus:
1. Before you script anything, check that the four channels' signal-side parts (the IS sense resistors/filters, the IN/DEN input parts, the LED drivers and their resistors) have the same relative placement and rotation. Report any differences.
2. Design one channel's bus (IS sense, IN/DEN input, LED lines) from its signal-column parts through the In2 corridor to D12-D15/U1, as a function in fixed_routes.py.
3. Generate the other three channels with that function, using per-channel offsets or a mirror. Where placement differs, use per-channel parameters rather than moving power parts.
4. Keep J6 (v1 as on main, or v2 from 8.18 if it then builds better), CAN, USB and the U1 fan-out as fixed routes.
5. Add the J3 VBUS route and a D3-A route (FB1.2 -> D3) from 8.18 together. They compete for In2 west of x 26.5.
6. Pre-check the fixed copper at 0 DRC errors, then build.

STAGE 4 - short links:
1. Let Freerouting fill what is left.
2. If after the export fix it still leaves links open across builds, script those links in fixed_routes.py and build again.

ACCEPTANCE (every build):
- 0 DRC errors and parity 0;
- the pour rules from stage 2;
- no signal on In1.Cu (EMC rule 3), buck SW/CB on F.Cu only, nothing across the CAN barrier or the antenna strip, no via in OUT1-B (decision 170);
- fewer unconnected items than the board.

AFTER THE LAST KEPT BUILD:
1. Run python3 tools/heat_budget.py --ambient 40 --currents 4,4,4,4 (decision 9) and report Tj.
2. heat_budget.py does not model the In2 area. State the VS-In2 area, the island count and that all thermal vias are inside it.
3. Run python3 tools/fix_check.py --role pcb-fixer --scope pdm-4ch. It checks: schematic unchanged, parity 0, 0 DRC errors, outline and holes unchanged, no bottom SMT.
4. Update STATUS.md and design-notes (new 8.19).
5. Record your own layout choices (export fix, channel bus geometry) as auto decisions in the fix block.

If items stay open, list them under 'blocked' (two-way) with the exact nets and the next scripted route.

ONE-WAY DOORS (stop, do not do, ask in the report):
- any change to F.Cu/B.Cu VS copper, the 16 A paths, the surge path or any other power-zone outline;
- a signal track through any power pour other than VS-In2, or on a layer other than In2 inside VS copper;
- VS-In2 split, losing more than 15 %, or a PROFET thermal via ending up outside it;
- the heat budget failing at 40 C;
- loosening a DRC rule or clearance to clear DSN violations;
- moving a PROFET, Q30/U30/D31, a connector, a hole or the outline;
- a bottom-side part;
- any schematic change.
